name: Internal Critique

objectives.text: Identify when a simple statement does not make sense because it says two opposite things, such as 'I never say anything'
Explain in their own words why a spring cannot pour out fresh and salty water at once and connect this to words that disagree with themselves
Retell Proverbs 26:4-5 in their own words as teaching that a wise answer neither copies foolish thinking nor leaves it unanswered
Practice asking 'How do you know that?' and 'Does that fit with what you said before?' in a classroom role-play
Explain from the parable of the wise and foolish builders how a way of thinking built on a weak foundation falls when it is tested
Explain from Romans that Scripture teaches all people know God and his moral law, so those who deny him still rely on truths that come from him
Identify examples of 'borrowed capital' in which a person who denies God still appeals to right and wrong, logic, or meaning
Explain the two steps of an internal critique drawn from Proverbs 26:4-5, standing on another view's assumptions for argument's sake and then showing where they lead
Analyze a self-refuting claim such as 'There is no absolute truth' or 'Only science gives knowledge' to show how it undermines itself
Distinguish among three kinds of internal failure in a worldview, logical contradiction, arbitrariness, and inconsistency between stated belief and actual practice
Explain Francis Schaeffer's method of 'taking the roof off' by pressing a person's presuppositions toward their logical conclusions
Analyze how a worldview that denies God struggles to account for calling anything truly evil when it raises the problem of evil as an objection
Apply questioning to expose an arbitrary claim by asking what basis the claim has within the speaker's own system of belief
Explain why the Reformed tradition pairs an internal critique of unbelief with presenting the Christian position on its own terms
Construct an internal critique of materialism showing how it undermines confidence in reason and moral responsibility
Evaluate a common charge of contradiction against Christianity by testing whether the Christian worldview is consistent on its own terms
Evaluate postmodern relativism for self-referential inconsistencies in its claims about truth and meaning
Critique a non-Christian worldview expressed in a film, novel, or essay by identifying where its author or characters live inconsistently with its stated assumptions
Compare the reductio ad absurdum approach of presuppositional apologetics with classical and evidential approaches and explain why Cornelius Van Til emphasized it
Create a written or spoken dialogue that carries out an internal critique with gentleness and respect and then presents the Christian answer

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (spotting nonsense, Proverbs 26:4-5, asking 'How do you know that?', the wise and foolish builders, borrowed capital, self-refuting claims, Schaeffer's roof-off method, morality and the problem of evil, arbitrariness, critiques of materialism and postmodernism, reductio ad absurdum). Dropped 'silly talk vs true talk' as a vague duplicate of the kindergarten objective. Reframed 'people who don't know God are confused' as a doctrinal claim grounded in Romans 1-2. Merged the generic 'defend the faith by showing systems collapse' into the critique objectives. Added objectives for distinguishing contradiction, arbitrariness, and practical inconsistency, pairing critique with a positive presentation, testing charges of contradiction against Christianity, critiquing worldviews in media, comparing apologetic methods, and conducting a gentle dialogue. Added verse-level Scripture anchors and Westminster Confession references where they state the doctrine. TAG and ultimate authorities are left to the sibling sub-topics.
